1.explanation: The search input in <SelectContainer> is rendered via <TextInput type='search' />, which ultimately uses the StyledTextInput styled component in StyledTextInput.js. Safari applies a default “searchfield” appearance that ignores padding unless overridden with “-webkit-appearance: textfield”. Currently plainStyle forces “-webkit-appearance: none” only when plain is true, and inputStyle does not handle search inputs specially. Thus the StyledTextInput component (and its plainStyle rule) must be updated to include “-webkit-appearance: textfield” (or remove the none) when type='search' so that Safari will apply padding correctly. The onInput method in SelectContainer triggers this search rendering, so the render path there is also implicated.
1.bug_scenario: In Safari the Select component’s search input collapses to its default search‐field appearance, ignoring padding and looking very small. The screenshots show a tiny search box in Safari (no padding) compared to a properly padded input in Chrome.

2.explanation: The StyledTextInput definition in StyledTextInput.js is the central styled-component that controls all <input> styling for TextInput, including search inputs. Safari’s default searchfield appearance strips out padding, so without explicitly setting -webkit-appearance: textfield (as was done in v1), the padding rules in inputStyle are ignored. To fix this bug, StyledTextInput must be updated to include a rule for search inputs that overrides the native appearance (e.g. adding “-webkit-appearance: textfield;” when props.type === 'search').
2.bug_scenario: On Safari, the Select’s built-in search input renders with almost no inner padding because Safari applies its native “searchfield” appearance, which ignores the padding rules. In v1 this was worked around by forcing -webkit-appearance: textfield on the <input type="search"/>. In v2 the TextInput/StyledTextInput component doesn’t override the Safari default, so the search box looks very small and cramped on Safari (see first image). In Chrome the padding is applied correctly (second image).
